title: Alpha tester report (record.json)
description: The machine-readable contract for one tester report. VERIFY_TESTER_REPORT.py enforces exactly this file (it reads the required lists, enums, patterns, and x-aliases from here, so the schema and the validator cannot drift), plus the cross-field rules a JSON Schema cannot express: the alias pairs must be equal; the artifact identity states must be coherent with the observed digest (VERIFIED and OBSERVED_UNVERIFIED require an observed digest inside the subject set, MISMATCH requires one outside it, MISSING requires none - and the intake alias artifactDigest must be absent, never the expected digest substituted); artifact_digest_verified true is only coherent with VERIFIED; and reviewer-side courtesy secret scanning mirrors the intake's credential classes. A record carrying fixtureClass TEST_FIXTURE_ONLY is never a report. The four intake-alias fields exist because the report must also pass the Phase 9 intake validation unchanged (qualification/phase9/tools/intake.py): testerId, date, environment, artifactDigest are the spellings that boundary checks. The tester classifies nothing technically unless they want to: findings[] is optional, and severity/user-impact are assigned later, outside the immutable report.

schema.description: names the contract version this record answers

tester_id.description: your cohort identifier (T-NNN). The only identity that enters evidence; the mapping to a person lives with the operator, outside the repository.

report_type.description: the kind of experience you are reporting. Your choice is preserved immutably; the project may classify further later, beside - never over - your words.

submitted_at.description: ISO 8601 date of the run you are reporting

journey.description: which journey this report is about (GETTING_STARTED.md); exploratory covers everything outside the five

artifact_claimed_by_tester.description: what you believe you were running, in your own words (e.g. the ISO filename or where you downloaded it)

artifact_digest_observed.description: the digest YOU computed from the bytes you ran, or null if you could not. Never copy the published digest here - the report records what you observed.

artifact_digest_verified.description: true only if you compared your observed digest against the published identity yourself

artifact_identity_status.description: ARTIFACT_VERIFICATION.md: VERIFIED needs your observed digest matching the identity; MISMATCH is itself an important report; MISSING is honest and keeps the report as unbound user evidence

environment_summary.description: one line: VM (hypervisor + version) or a PII-free hardware sketch. No hostnames that name you, no serial numbers.

machine_label.description: optional: YOUR label for this machine (machine-1, blue-desktop) if you test on several. Never a serial number.

steps.description: what you did, as far as you got. May be empty - a report without steps is still evidence.

user_observation.description: what happened, in your own words. Preserved verbatim, forever.

reproduction_steps.description: optional: only if you can reproduce it. A report without these is still evidence of your experience.

accessibility_technology.description: optional: assistive technology in use (screen reader + version, contrast/text settings, input method), volunteered

performance_measurement.description: optional: only if you measured something. Preserved as your measurement (USER_REPORTED) until the project independently validates it.

measured.description: optional: structured observations in the pinned Phase 8 template shape ({what, value, evidence})

userReported.description: optional: impressions in the pinned Phase 8 template shape ({aboutStep, impression}) - your words, kept as words

findings.description: optional: fill only if you WANT to classify. 'I could not install it' as user_observation is a complete report without this.

digest_computation.description: optional: the command you used to compute the digest, so the observation is reproducible

attachmentDigests.description: sha256 per attachment filename; the intake recomputes these from the ingested bytes and refuses a mismatch. Mask credentials before attaching anything (PRIVACY_POLICY.md).
